#en:
Stumbled across an unsecured maintenance terminal no one bothered to wipe before they scuttled us. I guess when the order came down to abandon ZT-7430, scrubbing logs was lower on the list than getting out alive. The whole event still feels like that: alarms, half-heard orders, a rerouted power surge through CIC, then we were burning hard for the nearest friendly hull, leaving a lot of questions behind in our wake.

Tonight I dug through what was left. Buried under system checks and training sims, I found transfer traces tied into places a combat ship has no business touching. Power usage spiking in quiet corners of New Atlantis, recalculated risk curves pointing straight down into the undercity, flagged in a way that looks like someone meant to come back and tidy up but never did. We ran scenarios based on those models without knowing whose lives they balanced.

I keep seeing the underbelly of Neon when I close my eyes, those cramped walkways where I first heard the name everyone whispers now. Back then it sounded like a story we told to make sense of seized accounts and frozen wages. Now, sitting in a dead SysDef shell with old code still humming in the dark, I am starting to think someone down below the pretty plazas is where this all converges next. Someone who learned early what happens when the numbers say you do not count.
zh:
我偶然撞上一台没上锁的维护终端——他们把我们弄沉之前没人费心去擦它。我猜当弃守 ZT-7430 的命令下来时，擦日志在清单上的位置比活着出去低。整件事至今仍给我这种感觉：警报、听了一半的命令、一次绕过作战信息中心的重定向电力浪涌，然后我们拼命朝最近的友方船体烧去，在身后留下一大堆问题。

今晚我翻检了剩下的东西。埋在系统自检和训练模拟底下，我找到了与一些战斗舰根本不该沾边的地点相连的转账痕迹。新亚特兰蒂斯安静角落里的用电激增，被重新计算的风险曲线直指下层城区，打上的标记看起来像有人打算回来收拾干净，却始终没回来。我们基于那些模型跑过各种情景，却不知道它们在权衡谁的性命。

我一闭眼就看见霓虹城的下层，那些逼仄的通道——我就是在那里第一次听到如今人人都低声念着的那个名字。那时它听起来像我们为了理解被扣押的账户和冻结的工资而自己编的故事。如今，坐在这具死去的星防队船壳里，听着旧代码在黑暗中还在嗡鸣，我开始觉得那些漂亮广场下方某个人，就是这一切下一步汇聚的地方。一个早就学会了当数字说你"不算数"时会发生什么的人。

#en: They tell me it is nothing, that weather is messy on the frontier and the satellites are old, and I should stop asking why three different colonies, in three different systems, use the same phrases when they talk about the sky going wrong. Out here at the outpost, folks come in dusted and tired, ask for water and a line home, and only when the room is half-empty do they mention how the clouds moved like they were being steered, how the forecast tickers lagged three days behind reality. Every time I press, they glance at the Ranger badge, then soften what they just said, shaving off the edges like they have been taught the hard way not to sound certain.\n\nI used to argue, loudly, in the mess about how command was ignoring the pattern. Lately I have noticed the people who did that before me transfer out or stop talking altogether. Now I keep my voice low too, mark up the incident board in pencil instead of ink. The liaison asked me today why I always request the storm reports, why I am chasing the same anonymous ship signature through half a dozen testimonies. I told him it was for a personal project. He nodded like he believed me and suggested, very gently, that I might want to be careful how I phrase things in my official notes. Apparently anyone who sounds too sure about the sky ends up reviewed by people who do not like surprises.
zh: 他们告诉我那没什么，边疆天气本来就乱，卫星也老旧，我该停止追问为什么三个不同星系里的三座聚居地，谈起天空出问题时用的是同样的措辞。在这座前哨站，人们满身尘土、疲惫地进来，要水、要一条回家的通讯线路，只有在屋里半空时才会提起云是怎么像被操纵一样移动的，天气预报滚动条是怎么落后现实三天的。每次我一追问，他们就瞟一眼游骑兵徽章，然后把刚说的话软下来，把棱角削掉，像他们吃过苦头，学会了别显得太确定。\n\n我以前在食堂里大声争辩，说指挥部在无视这个图案。近来我注意到，在我之前那样做的人要么调走了，要么干脆不说话了。如今我也压低声音，用铅笔而不是墨水在事件板上做标记。联络员今天问我，为什么我总是索要风暴报告，为什么我在半打证词里追同一个无名的飞船特征。我告诉他那是为了一个私人项目。他点点头，像信了，然后非常温和地建议我，或许该小心自己在官方笔记里的措辞。看来任何对天空显得太确定的人，最终都会被那些不喜欢意外的人审查一番。

#en: I keep replaying the numbers in my head, as if the math will suddenly confess. Route risk projection, claim probability, expected loss. All neat, all within tolerance, all signed off by people who smiled across a table in New Atlantis and told me GalBank takes care of its partners. Then I sat in that routing den on Gagarin and heard captains talk about the same "low-risk" lane we signed them onto, like it was a dare. Same bend, same blind patch, same rumor about a man who can squeeze the odds until ships crack.\n\nWeeks later I am alone on this transport, walking past pallets that were never meant to arrive, trying not to look too long at the pattern of damage on the hull feeds. Officially we lost guidance in a freak corridor fluctuation. Unofficially, the chatter in the underbelly of Neon says someone is selling lanes tuned to fail only for certain cargos, at just the right distance from just the wrong kind of outposts. When I pushed those rumors up the chain, I got polite shrugs and a suggestion to take some leave, maybe visit the Red Mile and "blow off steam." That is the part that sticks with me. The people who know the charts best are also the ones most eager not to know why our models keep pointing toward the same lonely crater, on the edge of nowhere, where a man who lives on probability can disappear into the roar of the crowd.
zh: 我在脑子里反复重放那些数字，仿佛算式会突然招供。航线风险预测、索赔概率、预期损失。全都齐整，全都在容差内，全都由一些在新亚特兰蒂斯隔着桌子微笑、告诉我盖尔银行会照顾自己伙伴的人签了字。后来我坐在加加林那间航路室里，听船长们谈论我们签给他们的同一条"低风险"航道，像那是一场挑战。同样的弯，同样的盲点，同一个关于某个能把胜算挤压到船只开裂之人的传言。\n\n几周后，我独自在这艘运输船上，走过一些本不该抵达的货板，尽量不去久看船体数据流上的损伤图案。官方说法是我们在一次诡异的走廊波动中失去了制导。非官方地讲，霓虹城下层的闲话说，有人在兜售只为特定货物量身定制的会出事的航道，位置恰好在离最不该靠近的那类前哨站刚刚好的距离上。当我把这些传言往上推时，得到的只是客气的耸肩，以及一句建议——休个假吧，去红里"放放松"。就是这一点让我挥之不去。最懂星图的人，也恰恰最急于不去知道，为什么我们的模型总指向同一座天涯边缘的孤独环形山；在那里，一个靠概率为生的人可以消失在人群的吼声里。

#en:
I keep replaying that run from three years back, the one no one writes down but everyone steers around. We were patrolling near a thin-atmo rock, nothing on the charts worth naming, when the grav shear started to sing through the hull. Not the usual shudder, either. This was a rhythm, like someone plucking a string the ship was resting on.

Nav said it was a localized anomaly and plotted a bypass. The junior tech next to me whispered that the pattern matched a corridor she had seen in an old sim at Jemison, then laughed it off like a bad memory. Command pushed us through the edge of it anyway. We came out clean, on schedule, and the log got stamped as routine. That night in the mess, nobody talked about how the stars had bent around us, or why the atmospheric telemetry from that nameless rock looked like it was expecting company.

Most of those people have shipped out to other billets by now. One took a payout and retired planetside, one signed on with Freestar haulage, a couple got themselves lost in Neon. They all moved on, thinking it was just another weird day in the black. I did too, until I saw the same pattern turn up in frontier distress calls, always near worlds with air too thin to argue with. Now there is an empty UC hull parked in that old anomaly, and someone else is following a line we traced without ever seeing where it led.
zh:
我一直在重放三年前那次航行——那次没人写下来、却人人绕开的事。我们在稀薄大气的一颗岩石附近巡逻，星图上没什么值得命名的东西，这时重力剪切开始透过船体歌唱。也不是寻常的震颤。那是一种节律，像有人在拨动飞船正停靠其上的那根弦。

导航说那是局部异常，画了一条绕行路线。我旁边那名初级技工低声说，那图案和她在杰米森一次旧模拟里见过的一条走廊吻合，然后像一段糟糕记忆一样一笑带过。指挥部还是把我们推过了它的边缘。我们干净地出来，准点，日志盖上了"例行"的章。那天晚上在食堂里，没人谈星星是怎么绕着我们的，也没人谈为什么那颗无名岩石传来的大气遥测看起来像在等人。

那些人如今大多已经调到别的岗位上去了。一个拿了一笔钱去行星表面退休，一个签了自由星系联盟的货运，还有几个把自己弄丢在霓虹城里。他们都往前走了，觉得那不过是黑色太空里又一个古怪的日子。我也一样，直到我看见同样的图案出现在边疆求救呼叫里，总是靠近那些大气稀薄得无从争辩的星球。如今一具空的联殖船壳停在那处旧异常里，而别人正在沿着一条我们描过、却从未看见它通向何方的线追下去。

#en:
I am logging this before I change my mind and dump the whole lot into the recycler.

The module is quiet now, just the hum of old cooling loops and one stubborn status light that refuses to admit the system is dead. I finally traced the breach tonight. Not the first intrusion, not the loud one everyone documented to prove they had done their jobs, but the thin hairline cut underneath it. Buried in a backup schedule, there is a redirect that should not exist, pointing asset updates to a GalBank vault ship that was supposedly decommissioned three fiscal years ago.

When I called it out in the team channel, nobody argued. They just went silent in that practiced way, the one that says they have seen this shape before and have all agreed to forget it. Same way they "forgot" the missing storm logs on that frontier moon. Same way nobody talks about the partial audio from the abandoned relay, the one where a voice tried to warn someone and then cut off mid-word.

So now I have a route number, a hull designation nobody uses out loud anymore, and a headache that feels a lot like complicity. The next piece is sitting in that drifting vault, wrapped in layers of old insurance law and newer lies. And when this is over, I am not sure which will be harder: proving what was done, or getting anyone to admit they always knew where the evidence was hiding.
zh:
我趁自己还没改主意、把这一整批全倒进回收机之前把它记下来。

模块现在很安静，只有旧冷却回路的嗡鸣，和一盏固执地不肯承认系统已死的状态灯。今晚我终于追出了那次入侵。不是第一次闯入，也不是那件被所有人记录下来好证明自己尽了职的大动静，而是它底下那道细细的发丝切痕。埋在一份备份计划里的，是一个本不该存在的重定向，把资产更新指向一艘据称在三个财政年度前就已退役的盖尔银行金库船。

我在团队频道里点出它时，没人争辩。他们只是以一种熟练的方式沉默了——那种"我们以前见过这种形状、并且都约好忘掉它"的沉默。就像他们"忘掉"了那颗边疆卫星上失踪的风暴日志。就像没人谈起那座废弃中继站上的一段残缺音频——里面有个声音试图警告某人，然后在半个词上被切断。

所以现在我有一个航路编号、一个再也没人大声说出的船体代号，以及一阵很像"同谋"的头痛。下一块碎片就在那座漂流的金库里，裹在层层旧保险法和更新的谎言中。等这一切结束时，我不确定哪个更难：证明做过了什么，还是让人承认他们一直知道证据藏在哪儿。

#en:
I was not supposed to be anywhere important that day. Just another junior tech checking latency on a half dead comms relay above some no name rock, arguing with a supervisor who kept mixing up time slots and routing codes. First miscommunication right there he swore my assignment was next week, I swore I heard "now," so I went anyway.

That is when I found the slate, half buried by the loading ramp, casing blackened like it had tried to die in a fire. I almost logged it as scrap, but the tag pinged our system in a way that did not match any of our manifests. I called it in, dispatcher said it was probably leftover survey junk, told me to wipe it and move on. She thought I was on a different shift, different sector. Second misstep.

I cracked it open on my own time. Most of it was static, but there was this fragment of traffic tied to a Trade Authority route and a firmware key that felt too sharp, too clean, to be random debris. I sent a copy to a contact in Neon, got an auto reply that did not sound like him at all flat, formal, as if someone had put the words in his mouth.

Since then small things keep slipping. People swear they answered a message they never saw, forget who told them a story about a woman who walks through vaults without touching anything. It feels like our whole lives are being edited one misheard instruction at a time.
zh:
那天我本不该出现在任何重要的地方。不过是又一个初级技工，在某块无名岩石上方检查一座半死的通讯中继站的延迟，跟一个老是把时隙和路由代码搞混的主管争论。第一次误会就在那儿——他赌咒说我的任务是下周，我赌咒说我听到的是"现在"，于是我还是去了。

就是那时我发现了那块数据板，半埋在装卸坡道旁，外壳烧得发黑，像它曾试图在火里死掉。我差点把它记成废料，可它的标签以一种不符合我们任何清单的方式打进了我们的系统。我上报了，调度员说那大概是勘测留下的垃圾，叫我擦掉继续干活。她以为我在另一个班次、另一个星区。第二次失足。

我在自己的时间把它撬开了。大部分是静电，但有一段与一条贸易管理局航线相关的数据片段，和一个固件密钥——那密钥太尖锐、太干净，不像是随机碎片。我把一份拷贝发给霓虹城的一个联系人，收到一封自动回复，完全不像他：平板、正式，像有人把话塞进了他嘴里。

从那以后，小事不断溜走。人们赌咒说自己回复过一条从没见过的消息，忘了是谁告诉过他们一个关于某个不触碰任何东西就走遍金库的女人的故事。感觉我们整个生活都在被一条条听错的指令编辑着。

#en:
Did not think I would ever come back to a place like this.

The relay bunker smells like stale coolant and dust, like the war hung up its coat here and forgot to leave. Most of the consoles are dark, but enough of the grid is still talking to itself that I could pry open the scan archive. The deserter who ran from this post knew what they were doing; the logs around the dates I needed were scrubbed so clean it hurt to look at them. No patrol chatter, no incident tags, just a neat band of silence where a whole flight's worth of traffic should have been.

Thing is, whoever did the cleaning missed the reflections.

Atmospheric scans bounce. You wipe the primary traces, you still get echoes in the background noise, ghost signatures where hulls pushed air aside. I layered the right bands, filtered for mass and vector, and there it was: the same drive profile I saw in that orphaned buoy's telemetry, sliding through restricted sky like it had every right to be there. It did not land on any registered pad. It just dipped low over a dead industrial zone and vanished off the board.

That zone feeds into a Deimos yard no one has funded in years, a scrapyard they pretend is shuttered but still keeps tug traffic in the middle of the night. Everybody in the bunker logs just called it "the graveyard" and left it at that. No one spelled out why. No one had to.
zh:
没想到我还会回到这种地方。

中继碉堡闻着是陈腐冷却液和灰尘的味道，像战争在这儿挂上了外套、忘了带走。大多数控制台都黑着，可电网还有足够多的部分在自言自语，让我撬开了扫描档案。从这个岗位逃走的那名逃兵知道自己是在干什么；我需要的那些日期前后的日志被擦得干干净净，看着都刺眼。没有巡逻闲聊，没有事件标记，只有一整条飞行量本该在的整齐的沉默带。

问题是，动手清理的人漏掉了反射。

大气扫描会弹回。你擦掉主痕迹，仍会在背景噪声里得到回响，得到船体推开空气处留下的幽灵特征。我把正确的频带叠起来，按质量和矢量过滤，它就在那儿：和我在那只孤儿浮标遥测里见过的同一副驱动剖面，滑过受限天空，像它完全有权待在那里。它没有降落在任何登记的停机坪上。它只是低低掠过一片死寂的工业区，然后从板上消失。

那片区域连着火卫二一座多年无人出资的船坞，一座他们假装已封闭、却仍在深夜接待拖船交通的废料场。碉堡日志里所有人都只叫它"墓地"，就此打住。没人说清为什么。没人需要说。

#en:
I keep replaying it in my head, all the tiny choices that felt harmless at the time.

The first time I let a route update slide even though the numbers did not quite match the weather feeds, it was because the shift was over and my eyes hurt. The second time, because the supervisor said the contractor knew more about storm lanes than we ever would. After that, it was habit. Click accept, file the correction, trust the invisible hand nudging freighters a few degrees off the safe corridors.

Nobody ever said his name in the control room. They just talked about "the vector guy," the one who could pull a ship through an ion front without losing a panel. The pilots were grateful, the accountants were thrilled, and we stopped looking too closely at the cuts in the safety margins because every successful run made the risk feel smaller.

Then one supply shuttle vanished between beacons and came back on a different heading with half its hull scorched and a manifest that did not match. We wrote it up as sensor interference and moved on. That was the moment, I think, when "just one more little adjustment" tipped into whatever this is now.

I am logging this because I can feel the pattern tightening around my station, and I cannot tell anymore if I helped build a safer route through chaos or just paved a road straight into it, one small approval at a time.
zh:
我在脑子里一遍遍重放它，重放所有那些当时觉得无害的微小选择。

第一次让一条航路更新溜过去，尽管数字和天气预报对不太上，是因为我下班了、眼睛也疼。第二次，是因为主管说那个承包商对风暴航道的了解比我们这辈子都多。之后就成了习惯。点下接受，归档修正，信任那只把货船推离安全走廊几度的看不见的手。

在控制室里，从没人说过他的名字。他们只说"那个矢量男"——那个能把一艘船拽过离子锋面而不掉一块面板的人。飞行员们心怀感激，会计师们乐不可支，而我们不再细看安全余量上那些削减，因为每一次成功航次都让风险感觉更小了一点。

后来一艘补给穿梭机在信标之间失踪了，回来时航向不同，半个船壳被烧焦，清单也对不上。我们把它写成传感器干扰，然后翻篇。我想，就是那一刻，"就再做一次小小的调整"滑进了如今这个不知叫什么的东西。

我记下这些，因为我能感觉到那图案正在我的站点周围收紧，而我已经分不清，我是帮着在混乱中修出了一条更安全的路，还是只是一次一次小小的批准，铺了一条直通它的路。
